headline: Every major above its 200-day and overbought, while whales quietly feed exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unusually clean today: six of seven majors sit above their 200-day trend line, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB and DOGE all in that camp, with only ADA below at 75.6% off its 12-month high. That's a market where the uptrend is broad, not a one-asset story. But broad doesn't mean calm. BTC is up 22.5% over seven days and 21.8% over thirty, ETH is up 30.7% over the week, and XRP has ripped 51% in seven days. This is a fast tape, not a grinding one.

Momentum confirms the trend almost too well. Every asset's MACD sits above signal, and RSI readings are stretched across the board: XRP at 86.9, SOL at 84.2, DOGE at 84.7, BNB at 84.3, BTC at 80.6. These are not gentle overbought readings, they're the kind of numbers a desk flags because moves this synchronized and this hot rarely extend forever without at least a pause. There's no bearish divergence here (price and momentum agree), but agreement at these RSI levels is itself the finding: everything is leaning the same way, hard.

Positioning tells a quieter story than the price action suggests. Funding across BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and DOGE is uniform at 0.01% per 8 hours (about 11% annualized), which is unremarkable, not the kind of expensive, crowded funding that usually accompanies a blow-off. Long/short ratios do show the crowd's lean: DOGE traders are long at 3.06 to 1, SOL at 1.99 to 1, XRP at 1.97 to 1. Yet liquidations skew short-heavy on the majors, ETH shorts lost $10.5M against $4.8M in longs over 12 hours, BTC shorts lost $8.5M against $5.8M in longs over 19 hours. Shorts are the ones getting run over here, which fits a market grinding higher against resistance.

Flows are where the tension actually lives. On 21 Aug, BTC spot ETFs took in $307.5M, part of a five-session run of $1,917.8M, all five days in the same direction. ETH ETFs added $184.0M that day, $692.6M over five sessions, same clean streak. That's real traditional-finance demand showing up day after day. Set against that: whale activity over the last 48 hours shows $230.5M net moving onto exchanges, led by $205.6M in BTC (including two single Binance deposits of $179.7M and $133.3M), plus $120M of USDC landing on Coinbase, arguably dry powder rather than a sell signal, but exchange-bound flow all the same. Zoom out to the weekly view and the pattern is consistent: the week ending Aug 16 saw $441M move onto exchanges, and the week ending Aug 23 saw $1,062M onto exchanges, a reversal from the $1,075M that left exchanges in the week ending Aug 02. Coins are migrating back toward venues where they can be sold, even as ETF buyers keep showing up with cash.

Sentiment reads Greed at 66, inside its 30-day range of 25 to 72, so the crowd is warm but not at an extreme. Stablecoin float is essentially flat over 30 days ($308.5B, +0.01%), meaning the sidelines aren't visibly refilling with fresh dollars even as prices run. Layer that against RSI readings in the 80s and exchange-bound whale flow, and you get a market where the retail gauge is only moderately greedy while the on-chain and momentum data are both closer to stretched. What to watch: whether the five-day ETF inflow streak holds or breaks, whether funding stays flat while OI grows (a sign of leverage building under an already-overbought tape), and whether the weekly whale flow flips back to net outflow from exchanges, the kind of shift that would mark coins moving back to cold storage rather than toward the order book.
